utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everybody. Everybody looks so far away. It looks like you are running away from the Bench. Mr. Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, and good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-83-T, the Prosecutor versus Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have the appearances, starting with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Good afternoon, Your Honours, Counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. For the Prosecution, Daryl Mundis, Kyle Wood, Matthias Neuner, our intern Emma Berry, and our case manager, Alma Imamovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to the learned colleagues from the OTP, everybody in and out of the courtroom. Appearing for General Delic, we have Vasvija Vidovic and assistant Lejla Gluhic and Lana Deljkic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Both teams have brought their entire forces today. Mr. Sljuka, yesterday, at the beginning of your testimony, you made a declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just to remind you that you are still bound by that declaration to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing else but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Questioned by the Court:

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, when we dispatched yesterday, you and I were talking about paragraph 40 of your witness statement to the Prosecution. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'll ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 273, please. Now, can we just have a look at the heading. The subject says: "The formation of the El Mujahedin Detachment in the 3rd Corps zone of responsibility," and the order is to the 3rd Corps Command. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we show the witness the end of the document, please. Can you see who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Staff commander of the Supreme Command, Mr. Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Had you been aware of this document before, before today?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now that you know of the document, do you have any comment to make on your statement at paragraph 40, where you say that the El Mujahedin Detachment was not in the command of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember all the orders based on which the El Mujahedin Detachment came into the area of responsibility of the 35th Division, but when I said this, I meant exclusively the following: That El Mujahedin Detachment did not honour the orders of the commander of the 35th Division and that he could not command that unit as he could command the other units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, let me hold you there. You are obviously -- we are now obviously talking at cross-purposes. This document doesn't talk about the 35th Division. It talks about the 3rd Corps. Okay? And it talks about the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment within the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps; okay? My simple question to you is: Now that you say you didn't know about this document before, what is your comment, if any, now that you are aware of the document, on paragraph 40 of your statement? Do you have any comment to make on that?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I could take a look at the paragraph 40 so I really know what it's all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: By all means. Can we supply the witness with paragraph 40 in the B/C/S, please. And I'm talking about the statement -- paragraph 40 of the statement that you made to the OTP on the 7th of July, 2006. I'm specifically asking for a comment on the statement that you are making that the El Mujahedin Detachment was not part of the army.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this is being interpreted, but my opinion is although there were some orders, the El Mujahedin Detachment did not observe those orders, they did not respect the Command of the 35th Division. They did things the way they wanted and what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you. I'm asking you to comment on paragraph 40. You are not mentioning the 35th Division in paragraph 40. Please, listen to my question, and if you don't have a comment, say, "I don't have a comment," but don't create a question for yourself and then answer the question.

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do apologise, but when I said -- when I mentioned "units," I mentioned the units within the AOR and within the composition of the 35th Division.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Paragraph 40 talks of ABiH. It doesn't talk of 35th Division. Please look at paragraph 40 of your statement. And if you can't answer my question, say you can't answer my question, but stop introducing foreign elements to the paragraph. You are a lawyer. You should be able to -- you and I should be able to communicate better, shouldn't we?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, but I'm not introducing anything new. The Army of BiH and the units of the Army of BiH, I really meant exclusively those within the composition of the 35th Division, because this is where I worked and these are the units I worked with, exclusively the 35th Division, and it had several units and several brigades.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I can't take the matter any further. That brings me to the end of my questions of you. Any questions arising from the questions by the Bench, Mr. Wood?

utterances.speaker: MR. WOOD
utterances.text: None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Further Cross-examination by Ms. Vidovic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, Witness, His Honour showed you at the end of your testimony, an order resubordinating the El Mujahedin Detachment to the Division. And now before you, you have a decision ordering the formation or the establishment of the El Mujahedin Detachment. This is what we see on paper; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These are just papers?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the de facto state of affairs in the ground? Was it not that the units of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina did not control the El Mujahedin Detachment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: HAMDIJA SLJUKA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. They were led by their own will. Nobody could control them.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. That brings us to the conclusion of your testimony, sir. Thank you very much for coming. Have a good trip back home. You are now excused. You may stand down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The Prosecution calls Edin Husic, and Mr. Husic will be led on direct examination by Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please make the declaration. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. You may sit down. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to you, sir. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you state your name, please?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: My name is Edin Husic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: When were you born, Mr. Husic?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 28th of April, 1967.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This is some information for the Chamber: Is it correct, Mr. Husic, that you testified for the Prosecution in the Kordic case?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you testified later on for the Defence of Enver Hadzihasanovic at this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the permission of the Chamber, I would lead the witness through his CV and military career.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, from 1982 until 1986, you attended the Military High School in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I attended the Military High School, which should be middle-ranking military school, not a military college.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And from 1986 until 1990, you were attending the Military Academy in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in 1990, you attended a one-year Intelligence Reconnaissance School outside Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you left the JNA at the end of 1991 -- excuse me. You left the JNA at the end of 1991, the beginning of 1992, holding the rank of lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a mistake in interpretation. It was said "1995", but it was at the end of 1991 and the beginning of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I misspoke. My apologies. And at the end of April 1992, you joined the TO in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And already by the end of June 1992, you were the chief of the Intelligence for the District Defence Staff in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And at the beginning of 1993, you joined the 3rd Corps as an intelligence officer?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Occasionally, while holding that position, you also served as a duty officer in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That's correct as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In June 1993, you became assistant to the Chief of Staff for Intelligence?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in the second half of 1994, you became the assistant commander for Intelligence in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my opinion, although I cannot specify the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: By mid-1996, you were assistant to the military attache of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Vienna?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in December of that same year, you were acting military attache of the BiH in Austria?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: From there, in December 1999 you moved to become an intel officer in the Federal Ministry of Defence of BiH?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And in August 2000, you became defence attache of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina to the United States of America?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I became defence or military attache of Bosnia-Herzegovina, not of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you for this clarification. At the beginning of 2006, you were the chief of Organisation and Mobilisation Department of the Joint Command of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And since March of this year, you were the chief of support office to the chief of the Joint Staff of the Armed Forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain to the Chamber what rank you're holding currently?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I hold the rank of a colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to take you to the period 1993, when you served as an intelligence officer. And as we have heard, at the 3rd Corps you occasionally performed the duty of duty officers. Could you explain what a duty officer does?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Duty officers usually held their post for 24 hours. They worked in the Operations Centre or in a separate special room, from where they could monitor and follow the situation within the area of responsibility. They were duty-bound to report on more significant events to the commander or deputy commander immediately, if required or necessary, and if there were regular activities going on where there were no urgent needs to report, then duty officers would report at the end of their shift.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want --

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Just a moment. Reporting was based on reports of subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to show you one of the reports from subordinated units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could have PT1093 be shown to this witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, just before we go on to this document, can we just understand the transition here. My understanding was that a duty officer is on duty and observing, and he reports events that are significant, if any. And then he says, "And if there were regular activities going on where there were no urgent needs to report, then duty officers would report at the end of their shift." Now, I would expect that what they report is what they observed. Now, the next sentence that says: "Reporting was based on reports of subordinated units," I don't see how it relates to the rest of what he has been telling you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, you were serving at the 3rd Corps. Could you clarify what you put in your reports, being the duty officer at the 3rd Corps? Your own observations or other observations?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Reporting was based on reports provided by subordinated units. I do not understand this part of the question when it concerns my position or any officer who held that post of duty officer. We cannot observe anything. We are in a position to receive reports. When I say "monitor," I mean monitor on the basis of reports from others. And when I said "immediate reporting," I depicted situations where urgent reporting was necessary because of the situation. And when regular or ordinary activities were going on where there were no changes or where the situation did not necessitate urgent reporting to the commander, then reporting was done at regular intervals, at specified times, when they were then processed. We did not have any capabilities to report in the same form that we received such reports from subordinated units. We could not alter any content from units' reports. And at the end of the day, we were duty-bound to prepare our report that was sent to the commander and the Chief of Staff of the Corps. I hope that I've managed to clarify this matter to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have indeed, sir. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Would you now look at the report on the left-hand side in front of you. Could you tell me whose handwriting that is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we, for a second, in the B/C/S move to the second page. If you look at the end of your handwriting, I see two signatures. Could you explain whose signature is the signature on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The right-hand side signature is mine. The one to the left, I presume that is the one you are interested in. Are you asking me whose handwriting it is that is on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The signature on the left-hand side is the signature of the Chief of Staff of the Corps at that time, Mr. Muradif Mekic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So the Judge asked you a moment ago about the reporting, and you explained extensively about it. Could you explain what you're doing here, because Mr. Mekic has signed, obviously, what you wrote here?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I fail to understand part of the question. However, I will try to provide an answer concerning Mr. Mekic's signature. It was standard procedure that the Chief of Staff would sign a report at the end of the day indicating that he was acquainted with the information contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And information contained in that report, from whom did you receive that information which you put here in this report?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: From the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Subordinated -- units subordinated to whom?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: To the Corps Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Of which corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I ask that the document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 628.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on now to your duties and tasks as assistant commander for Intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain, in 1995, to whom were you reporting to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: In 1995, to the 3rd Corps commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Was this the only person or entity to whom you were reporting to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: At the Corps Command, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Did you report also to somebody outside the Corps Command?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: We were obliged to report the intelligence administration of the Staff of the Supreme Command at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who was the head of the Intelligence Administration of the Supreme Command Staff in 1995?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It was the late General Mustafa Hajrulahovic, Talijan.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to show to you, since we are talking about reporting, a document, PT2111. We can see here it's a document from the 27th of May, and if we could scroll down the B/C/S a little bit, please, to see the signature. Could you say who signed the document?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I signed this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if we look at number 1 of what you're reporting here, we see, I think it's the second paragraph, that during some combat activities, 30 Chetniks had been killed and that "the El-M Detachment holds captured aggressor soldiers and a tank." Could you first of all explain what "El-M" means?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The acronym stands for "El Mujahid."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you look for a moment at the distribution list of your document, could you explain what are you doing here with the document -- with the information about the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document must be scrolled down a little bit so that the distribution list is visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: In the B/C/S version, please, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And also in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Sorry, also in English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The distribution list is at the top of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could we scroll it up a little bit? Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your question is unclear to me. This report contains some other information as well, not only the ones pertaining to the El Mujahid Detachment. Irrespective of that, I will try to clarify. This document bears the title "Information on Enemy." That type of information was sent to all subordinate units and to all adjacent units as a circular letter. Such documents were there to inform on the events within the AOR in order to assist the subordinate and adjacent units to get a full picture of the situation as it was within the Corps AOR. In turn, it assisted them to interpret the information they gained more correctly in order to assess the situation in the most appropriate way and to try and forecast what would ensue. We see here Command of the 3rd Corps Intelligence Detachment; and the 37th Division Intelligence Department; brigade commands of the 1st and 2nd Manoeuvring Battalion, to their intelligence organ; and the forward command post; as well as the 3rd Corps Postojna, attention Ibrahim Begagic. Those were the adjacent and subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And where is Mr. Begagic working, in terms of to which section of the 3rd Corps does he belong to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Mr. Begagic worked in the Intelligence Department of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I see here the document has, on the upper right-hand side, the addition "Hitno." Could you explain what "Hitno" stands for and why you considered this document to have this addition, "Hitno"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I suppose that at the time, there were combat activities. As you may well know, or perhaps not, but usually during combat activities the situation can change quickly. Therefore, it is essential that intelligence information that one has at his disposal be forwarded to the end users.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I just note here the English translation doesn't contain the word "Hitno." Does"Hitno" mean urgent?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What does "Hitno" mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What does "Hitno" mean? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Was that a question for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the misunderstanding. "Hitno" means as early as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation, can I ask the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 629.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to take you now to September 1995. Could you tell me which combat operation, if any, took place in September 1995 in the 3rd Corps AOR?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: In September, at least according to the documents we were processing at the time, Operation F was in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what Operation F means?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The "F" stands for "Farz," as we called it. The end goal of the operation was to liberate the area of Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could, please, document PT2349 be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What role, if any, did you have in relation to Operation Farz?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: During Operation Farz, my task was to plan the measures for supporting intelligence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the document in front of you, could you explain --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we zoom in a little bit, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: -- what we see here in front of us? I see the words "Intelligence Support Plan." Could you explain to the Trial Chamber what an intelligence support plan is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: What we see -- or rather what I see before me is an intelligence support plan. It is a document which in all likelihood is a version -- the version of a plan. It's a proposal, since it wasn't signed, and the temporal reference is not mentioned. It was probably a working version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I see, in the upper right-hand side, "Operacija F." Could you explain again what Operacija F stands for?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Operation F means "Farz," as I've said already and as we refer to it, the goal was to liberate the area of Vozuca.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who produced this intelligence support plan?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Intelligence support plans were prepared by the Intelligence Department of the 3rd Corps for the needs of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So who initiated that such a plan be produced?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: We worked on orders issued by the corps commander, his orders and his instructions, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What is the name of the corps commander, please?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: At the time, the corps commander was Brigadier Sakib Mahmuljin; the 3rd Corps, I mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. If we look at the B/C/S on the fifth page, please, and in the English on page 6, we see here the heading is "Other," and I want to point your attention to number 2, which says: "The focus of intelligence support should be on the following axis: Svinjasnica, Paljenik, Stog, Miljevici, Vozuca." If I were to give you a map, would you be in a position to point out where this axis is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I'll do my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, if this could please be placed on the ELMO. Could we zoom out a little bit. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you, first of all, indicate where Svinjasnica is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Svinjasnica?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you could mark a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second, Mr. Neuner. Is this map from the map book?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's from the map book, but I notice the witness has a document in front of him, so it would collide to show both at the same time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, no. I want to know which map number in the map book.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: It's map 11, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle Svinjasnica and mark a "1" next to it, please? For Your Honours, the ERN is 0618-6706 of map 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you now, from Svinjasnica, mark an arrow towards Paljenik, Stog and Vozuca?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, perhaps my learned friend could explain to us what the purpose of the arrows should be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just trying to visualise the axis of intelligence support as stated here in the report under number 2. I was discussing this in the last two minutes with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you happy, Madam Vidovic?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you now mark an arrow from Svinjasnica via Paljenik, Stog, towards Vozuca, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Before I do that, there was a misinterpretation. The focus of the axis of intelligence support, this is what this should represent. Paljenik [indicates] --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you maybe, since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, would it be helpful for the witness to circle these places and perhaps give "1" to the first place, "2" to the next?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark Paljenik, which you just underlined, could you encircle it and mark a "2" next to it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you have the "1" next to the first one?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: This has already been done, Your Honour, on the upper right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you encircle Paljenik, please, and mark a "2" next to it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And now encircle Stog and mark a "3" next to it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And encircle Vozuca and mark a "4" next to it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Miljevici is also along this axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you find Miljevici, mark a "4" then next to Miljevici.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And encircle Vozuca then, please, and mark a "5" next to it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I want to ask you now about number 3 of your intelligence plan, in which it states: "Special attention should be paid to the interrogation of prisoners of war." Could you explain what you mean by this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It reads here that: "Special attention should be paid to interrogation of the prisoners of war or deserters or those who fled to the other side, collecting enemy documentation which should be delivered to the 3rd Corps forward command post in the village of Luka ASAP in order to be analysed." What we meant by this is special attention should be paid to the interrogation of POWs and deserters and to collect documentation, since we deemed those information sources to be important.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With this explanation, can I ask that document PT2349 be tendered into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document PT2349 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 630.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If now the next document, PT2544, could be shown to the witness, please. Could we scroll down so that the witness can see the signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you tell us whose signature that is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And if you just look at the bottom for a second, you see in handwriting here something. Could you read out what that meant, because it's difficult to read.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It reads: "10SAP0.PK."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It is the file name in its electronic version.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could scroll upwards, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here the date is the 9th of September, 1995. If we could just for a second, in the B/C/S, go to the second page. And read this together with the previous remark we just discussed on page 1, on the bottom. If you could go back to page 1 of the B/C/S, please. Yes. If you look again, what is the correct date of this document? Could you please try to help me?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It is most likely that this is the 10th of September. However, the handwritten note on page 2 that was just shown, and I see that for the first time, I don't think that is in my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is the handwritten note on the first page in your handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you notice that the document, at the top, is dated the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe if we can clarify. If you look at the first sentence of this document, and it's in the English to be scrolled down a little bit, yes, it talks here about: "... Combat operations as planned by our forces commenced at 6.00 in the direction of Seona, Stog, Vozuca." Could you tell us what day did the combat start, the 10th or the 9th of September, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I cannot tell you that unless you show me another document corroborating that, since I do not remember. In this document, there is obviously a difference in terms of dates. We don't have the date and the time. We only have the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But we have the time when it was processed, didn't we?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, we do. If, at the bottom, it says the 10th of September, and if it was saved as a file under that name, then that file was created on the 10th of September on the computer.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 631.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to PT2541.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Since this is depicted now, could you tell -- sorry. If you could scroll it down a little bit so that we can see the type-sign. We see it's type-signed only, and your name is mentioned. If you look at the document in its entirety, if it could please be zoomed out a little bit, do you recognise the document?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: If you could zoom in, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Zoom in a little bit again.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The document that I saw during proofing. If you could go back a bit, because I can see only a small portion of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You report here, and this is in English, please, on the second page, if we could go to the second page. In the -- in English, it's the second page, the second paragraph. In your B/C/S version, the third paragraph. You report here, among others: "One of our units reached the Ribnica sector by road from Stog via Vozuca and linked up with the forces of the 2nd Corps."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Neuner, where are you reading? On the second page, the second paragraph, if that is the second paragraph, says: "1 enemy T-55 tank was destroyed in the Ravne village sector."

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you count this one line as one paragraph, then it would be the third paragraph. I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Then the next one says: "Our forces succeeded in taking control of the entire area ..." It doesn't say what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The next sentence exactly says what I was referring to in the middle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, then you've got to say you're starting in the middle of the paragraph. Otherwise, we start at the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay, I will read out the entire sentence of concern: "The area and populated areas along the road have been abandoned, and we were told about it by one of the units which reached the Ribnica sector by road from Stog via Vozuca and linked up with the forces of the 2nd Corps." Do Your Honours find that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. I waited for the interpretation to finish. I object on grounds that the witness has not recognised the document yet. He sought the document be shown to him, and then he was interrupted by the Prosecutor's question which suggested "you report" in this report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to ask some general question about the document first before I come back to that paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, let's try to do that every time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the layout of the document, Mr. Husic, namely, on the first page, if you could scroll up a little bit, the reference to the Intelligence Department of the 3rd Corps Command, would that document in general reflect a typical document from the Intelligence section at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I notice that it is sent -- or, sorry, that the location is Zenica.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Do you know whether you have been in Zenica on the 9th of September?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: If it's written there, then I suppose I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's what that document says. Did you write this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot confirm that. Could you show me the whole document so that I can see it through?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you hear that, Mr. Neuner?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Could we please zoom out.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be barely seen, but it is possible to make out and for me to say that this is an electronic version of the document. What is customary is to the left of the signatory of the document, there should be the initials of that person. They are not present here. Given that there are no initials, there is not my signature, how can I confirm that this is my document or that I drafted it? This is not contentious in terms of its form or format, but if you ask me to be precise about it and given that there is -- it bears no initials and no signature, then I cannot confirm that it is mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the upper part, it says: "Processed on," on the second line here, "Sunday, 10 September, at 1834 hours." Does that help you a little bit, together with a file name maybe, to assess the validity of that document?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: The name of the file doesn't mean anything to me, because we did not assign names to files. Secondly, as to this time of Sunday, the 10th of September, and then there's an unintelligible bit and then "1834 hours," that just tells us when this document was processed, meaning when it was processed at the Communications Centre and when it was sent to the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So you can confirm that the document was sent to some addressees; yes?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It is written so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If I could, with this explanation, go back to the content for just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We discussed this paragraph mentioning Ribnica sector and that "one of our units," as the document states, "reached that Ribnica sector." Could you, on the map next to you, indicate where that Ribnica sector is?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I will try to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you have just encircled it, and could you please place a "6" next to the Ribnica sector?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I, with this last marking, ask that the map be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 632.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And could I also ask that the document PT2541 is now being tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I believe that a sufficient basis has not been established for this document to be admitted through this witness, because the witness has not recognised it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I believe the witness has in general stated that the format of the document is one which comes from his intelligence service or is similar to the one which his intelligence service at the time used. The witness has also stated clearly that the document was indeed sent, though type-signed as it is in front of us today. And the witness has also acknowledged the content of that document, meaning that he's familiar with the Ribnica sector and could mark it on a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, is format one of the factors to ground admissibility of a document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I didn't want to suggest that format alone is one of the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I'm taking them one by one. I'm coming to the next one. The next one, you're saying he confirmed that it is sent. He said it says so. That's what he was reading on the document, it says it was sent. He doesn't express independent knowledge that it was sent to the addressee.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I wish to say that the document is also type-signed for the witness. I acknowledge that there is no signature on it. During our attempts to seize it from the archive, this was the best copy we could get at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand, sir, but the very fact that it is type-signed, isn't that a difficulty, a hurdle that you must go over, by at least more recognition of the document by the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, it was sent in this form, meaning electronically processed, and we had a couple of documents in this trial which were not signed by every witness, but since they were sent, as this document, in electronic form, they didn't bear any signatures of the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That is true, Mr. Neuner, but those witnesses were in a position to identify the document and take ownership of it. This witness says the file number on this document means nothing to him because they didn't assign file numbers to documents, and that it was processed on the 10th of September at 1634 with unintelligible writing in between means nothing to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm prepared to ask the witness about another paragraph of this document and ask him to confirm -- and Your Honours will see that in this other paragraph, there are some places mentioned which feature prominently throughout the following documents which this same witness has also authored. I can lay a foundation here for these place names and can then ask the witness for other documents which he signed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Your opposite number is on her feet. Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. Your Honour, the Prosecutor has already explained to the witness what he is supposed to confirm from this document, so this is leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stand up, Mr. Neuner. You see, the problem is that procedurally we're supposed to establish ownership of the document or admissibility of the document before we go to the contents. By the time we go to the contents, the document should be in the position to be admitted at that stage. To try to say this witness knows about the document because he knows the contents, he might have an independent knowledge of those incidents because he was in that area, not because he's the author of the document. Do you understand the difference?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. Your Honour, I was indicating a moment ago that I would be prepared to ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But this is the point, and then your opposite number says, "You're beginning to lead your witness, you're telling the witness what you're going to be establishing," and that's what you're not supposed to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: So what does Your Honour want me to do, then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I want you to lay a proper foundation for admission of the document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you suggest --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm not --

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the time, if I could suggest that we are making a break, and I will try to revisit the document after the break, then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Shall we mark it for identification in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, the document is marked for identification. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI633.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'll take an adjournment and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, have you resolved your problem?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to refer to another document first, and I might revert to that document later which was discussed before the break. I want to go to PT2543 now, please. If you could scroll up a little bit, yes, so Mr. Husic can see.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My first question is: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Husic, if you look at the first sentence, please. If the English could be scrolled down a little bit so that the Judges could see. Yes, thank you. There is mentioning made of a Prokop sector, where 2nd and 3rd Corps forces converged. Would you be in a position to find Prokop on a map?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I'll try to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. If you could please have map 17 of the Court binder with an ERN of 0618-6712 shown to the witness. I also have a hard copy, if it would assist, because the witness is still looking at the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, I'm advised that that map can be put up on e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At the same time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, certainly not at the same time. Okay, I guess Mr. Neuner wants to have this document on e-court and the map on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes. There are a couple of documents which refer to this map. If you please --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want us to look at at this point in time, the map or the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: At the map, please. The document, I've read the relevant passage into the record, convergence of 2nd and 3rd Corps Corps -- forces of the 3rd Corps -- convergence of these forces in the Prokop sector, and I want the witness to point out to Your Honours where is this Prokop line. If we could, please, enlarge a little bit the area shown on the ELMO. Zoom out a little bit. If we zoom out. It's not possible? Then if you move the map a little upwards. Yes. Actually, the other way around. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mr. Husic, would you be in a position to find Prokop, where the forces joined, the 2nd and 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, you have encircled it, and could you mark a "1" next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're stating in your document that: "The convergence at this point in time marked the end of the liberation of the larger Seona-Stog-Vozuca sector." Could you explain what you meant by this at the time?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It was considered, as far as I wrote, that the completion of the liberation of the larger Seona-Stog-Vozuca sector and by the linking up of these forces, it was considered that this area had been liberated.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: By which forces liberated?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It is written here that the forces of the 2nd and 3rd Corps linked up in the area of Prokop. It doesn't state which exact units are those. These are units of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And when you say "this area had been liberated," which area are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is spelt out. The liberation of the larger area of Seona-Stog-Vozuca. The next sentence described that there is the establishment of authorities underway in Vozuca, and this is the area which is marked out here. I don't know how other way should I put it or explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. We were looking at the map, and we can only see the map at one time. Now we have seen your document. Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could I ask that the document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 634.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If we could move on to the next document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... With the map, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: The map will stay for the moment. I'm aware about it. PT2550. Your Honours, while the document is being shown, I note the time. I will still have a few documents for this witness, but I'm trying to be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: We see here it's a document from the 2nd Corps IKM, Intelligence Department, and if you please look at the receiver for a moment. If we could scroll down in the B/C/S, please. I think it's the last page in the English. My question for you, Mr. Husic, is: Did you receive or see that document?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I presume that I did, since it is addressed to the department that I headed.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Okay. So if we look in the middle of the B/C/S, first page, at the sentence starting with: "Na odsijeccenom dijelu teritorije ... " And in English that's the second page, there on the second page in English, the third paragraph, and the sentence starts: "There are still many enemy soldiers on the part of the territory that is cut off. We have information that there is a group of 100 Chetniks in the area of Prokop who want to surrender to the units of the 2nd Corps. That piece of information is still being verified." My question to you is: Here is mentioning of Prokop. What location is mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Prokop is being mentioned here. This is what it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: To avoid any confusion, is that the same Prokop we talked about a moment ago where the 2nd and 3rd Corps forces converged?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I presume that this is so. This is not my document, however, but I do presume that this is so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can I ask that the document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 635.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I want to move on to PT2584.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Before it's enlarged, could we please ask you: Whose signature is this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And we see it's from the 12th of September. The location is Luke. Could we please look at the fifth paragraph on the B/C/S. In English, it is page 2, the last paragraph there in English. If you could, in English, move to page 2, please. Yes, the last paragraph, please, and I think it's the third line in English which mentions: "Broken-up groups of Chetniks numbering between 40 to 60 from the 14th lpbr are probably in the Kablovac, Prokop and Stoska Kamenica sectors." Do you find this?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Can you explain what "lpbr," the "14th lpbr" stands for?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: It stands for the 14th Light Infantry Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And I want to walk -- or I want to ask you now to indicate the place names you have mentioned here in your document. Prokop, it's not necessary, since we have it already. If you look on the map next to you, would you find Kablovac which you're mentioning in your document?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I'll try.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, because I think the witness might mark on the special area. Yes, he's moving it himself already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Just encircling it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you mark a "2" next to Kablovac, please?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you. And would you find the Stoska Kamenica sector?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Please mark a "3" next to it. You have just encircled it.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The witness is supposed to mark Kamenica or Stoska Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: He's marked it with a "3".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I know he's marked it, but is he marking Kamenica or Stoska Kamenica? Your question at line 32: "And would you find the Stoska Kamenica sector?" Where is Stoska?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Where is Stoska? You have circled Kamenica.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: This is Kamenica [indicates]. As for Stoska Kamenica, I cannot see it on the map. But I encircled this name, "Kamenica," because we were looking at this part of the map. It may be that on a different map, it would read differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what "Stoska" stands for?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I'm not here to interpret toponyms and their meaning. It may be a reference to a particular location, but I am truly no expert in this region.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My understanding is, nevertheless, you have reported about the two other locations, Prokop and Kablovac here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And on that basis I would ask that the document please be tendered into evidence, the document PT2584.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 636.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I now want to revert back to the document marked for identification, 633. This was the document which was type-signed only, we discussed before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look there, please, at the fourth paragraph in the B/C/S version. In English, it is the second page, the third paragraph. It talks here about: "Based on the information on the lines reached by the 2nd Corps, we estimate that part of the enemy forces, at a strength of one reinforced infantry battalion, are in the general areas of Kosa village, Pejanovici village, Prokop, Crni Vrh and Kamenica village." Could you, by looking at the map, explain where these locations are?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: I'll try to do so. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're encircling "Kosa" right now. Could you please mark a "4" next to it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're encircling "Pejanovici" right now. Would you please mark a "5" next to it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're encircling again "Prokop." Maybe for the record, this has already a "1" next to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You're encircling Crni Vrh. Could you please mark a "6" next to it?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And you're, in a way, again encircling "Kamenica" which has a "3" next to it, yeah. Having just looked at the other documents and now looking at this document again, what would be your comment about this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Could you please clarify your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: You have just highlighted for us the place names stated in the document we were discussing earlier, marked for identification 633. What would your explanation about that particular paragraph which is made here in this document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. First of all, the Prosecutor is leading the witness as to which locations to encircle, and the witness followed. Based on that, based on being prompted by the Prosecutor, the witness is now again being asked to interpret a particular paragraph. I truly fail to understand what the purpose of this line of questioning is.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have asked an open question to this witness, asking him to give an explanation if he's in a position to do so. I didn't intend to lead him in any way. It is clear to me, from the answers given by this witness, that he recognises the place names, but I was asking this time a very open question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Neuner, you should have shown that there is a connection between the witness and the document. You should have demonstrated this, because I do not see such a connection. As we're speaking, I do not see a connection between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let me just explain that to you. What you have demonstrated is a connection between the document and the map, not the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: But this witness is obviously in a good position to recognise all these places, and the witness -- the document is type-signed for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, if I can read and write, and you give me this map and you give me this document and you read to me the names in the document, and you say, "Find them on the map," do you think it would be difficult for me to find them? And if I did find them, does that establish a connection between me and the document? Anybody who can read can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, but I'm trying to elucidate what is in one of these paragraphs written in the document, and I just now, before I got the objection, asked a very open question, if the witness would be in a position to give a general explanation about it. I did not say that he should say this or should say that. I just asked him whether, after he had found the places, he could give an explanation what is written in this document. And depending on his answer, we may find a link or we may not find a link. I cannot presume at this point in time that there is a link. I can only ask the witness about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, if you had listened to Madam Vidovic's objection, it was to the effect that you led the witness to encircle names on the map, not the question that you asked, and then she says, Based on that, if asked the witness, 'Can you see this paragraph, it mentions this name and that name and that name, can you find the names on the map,'" and the witness finds a name on the map, and based on that, you now want to say there is a link between the witness and the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I do not wish to say that because I don't know the witness's answer yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Fair enough, but you're asking him to say, to comment on the document based on the fact that he has identified names on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm prepared to ask the witness about another portion of this document, if this helps, Your Honour, to get a link established. I do not need to ask about this particular paragraph, Your Honours. I can move on to another paragraph of that document. In all fairness, I must be allowed to ask about a paragraph in this document and see what the witness's answer is, and otherwise I'm prevented to move any further with regard to that document. Then it would stay in the situation in which it is, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Let me put the question to you this way, sir: Whatever the answer the witness is going to give to your question, what is your intention? Are you still going to go ahead and lay a foundation?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I have asked the witness about formal features of this document, of this document, and the witness has given certain answers. I understood from Your Honours that this was not satisfactory at this point in time, so I was prepared, after the formalities of this document have been dealt with, to ask about the content of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Which I'd indicated to you, before we broke up, that procedurally, before you go to the content, you must have laid the foundation. The document must be ready for admission before you deal with the content, because by the time you deal with the content, it is because the document is now admitted, now you're allowed to tender that into evidence and therefore you can begin to deal with the contents in the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I fully --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But -- yes, you fully?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I fully agree with Your Honours, but I have dealt with practically all formalities contained in this document; that it is from the 3rd Corps Command, from the Intelligence Department. The witness said, "Yes." That it was sent, that it looks similar to a document produced by the intelligence service at the time. The witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But those aren't foundational questions, Mr. Neuner, those are not foundational questions. Anybody who can read can see it does come from the 3rd Corps. Anybody who has seen a previous document from the 3rd Corps can see that it does like documents from the 3rd Corps. You don't need to have come from the 3rd Corps to see that, as long as you have seen previous documents from the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I understand, but this witness was even in the Intelligence Department, the letterhead of which is here in this document, so why should I not ask him about it, because it looks obviously that this is a link.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just put your question to the witness, the question that you were putting when Madam Vidovic stood up. Let's hear what the answer is and let's see where we go from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: My question was: I wanted to understand, apart from the locations just mentioned here, what is your explanation about this particular paragraph which talks about information reached by the 2nd Corps, information on the lines reached by the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: All I can do is provide you with an opinion of mine that I can have after having read the document. However, I do not see the link between this document and the other document stemming from the 2nd Corps. If you read this, it says: "Based on the information on the lines reached by the 2nd Corps, we estimate that part of the enemy forces, the strength of one reinforced infantry battalion, are in the general area of Kosa village, Pejanovici village, Prokop, Crni Vrh and Kamenica village." What would you like me to say, how I see this? Well, to me this is clear. This is an estimate based on certain information that had to do with enemy forces, the strength of one battalion in the area. I don't see what other clarification I could offer, since I cannot change the gist -- the meaning of the paragraph as written.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Who, in the Intelligence Department, is in a position to make an estimation?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Anyone who previously worked on the document, depending on who authored the document. From this document, since there was a question put by the Judges, I cannot confirm that I drafted this document, since that cannot be discerned from the looks of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Neuner, sorry for interrupting, but you just told us that the witness would have confirmed that the document had been sent. Could you please give us the reference in question, because in fact if this confirmation was a fact, maybe we could establish a link, but I do not see it. I do not see the link in the transcript. I do not see the confirmation. On page 25, line 20 -- [In English] "I notice that it is sent -- or, sorry, that the location is Zenica." [Interpretation] So I do not see this confirmation that the document -- that the witness can confirm that the document had been sent maybe somewhere else? The witness confirmed it, I don't know, on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I don't have the transcript in front of me, but if we could look at the first page, at the upper part of it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: If you look at the first two lines, could you explain, having worked in the Intelligence Service at the time, what the first two lines refer to?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could we see the English, please.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Do you mean beginning with the words "File name" and "Processed"?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: That part was not done by us, the Intelligence Department. It was done by the Communications Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And having worked still at the time in the Intelligence Service, would you at least have a general understanding what these two lines refer to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: These two lines refer to the file name and the time the file was processed, that's it, and so it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: What do you mean by "the file was processed"?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: "Processed," it means it went through the Communications Centre. That was the note they would make.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which communications centre are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: Of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Mentioning is also made in this document about an enemy tank. This is, in English, on page 2, the second paragraph, and in the B/C/S it is, so to speak, the third paragraph. What is meant by an enemy tank T-55?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: They refer to a tank.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Could you explain what "enemy tank" refers to?

utterances.speaker: EDIN HUSIC
utterances.text: "Enemy tank" means a tank in the possession of enemy forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: And which enemy forces are envisaged here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. I believe that these few questions concerning a tank, one could ask a whole lot of such questions, and it only results in wasting our time. The judicial economy is being put into question. I cannot see how questions such as this one can lead or amount to anything in order to establish any link with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner. Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I will abandon to ask further questions about this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Neuner, please, we have spent a very, very long time on this document now, and I am increasingly curious to know what was the purpose. So before we let you off the hook, I think you should explain to the Chamber, at least, what all this was about, because I, for one, am completely left in the dark about the importance of this document, which you, yourself, seem to have attached a great importance to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Should I do this in the presence of the witness? I'm prepared to do so, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Well, you hold the key to the secret. I don't know. If you think the witness should not hear what you have to say about it, then we can ask him to leave, but I think that you owe it to the Chamber to explain the importance and the significance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Maybe if I can ask that the witness is removing his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: He probably speaks English if he spent time in Washington. But, I mean, is it something that he cannot hear?

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: I'm fine, if Your Honours wish me to go ahead. This document is a part of a series of documents which are shown today to this witness, and they all relate to an area which is very close, as you can see on the map which was marked right now, which is very close to Kesten village, and it is relating to an area where -- or to a time period, all the documents we are showing, to a time period in which, as alleged in the indictment, on the 11th of September certain enemy soldiers were indeed captured, and through the several documents shown today, the intention was to demonstrate that there was almost an advanced knowledge of at least the Intelligence Service on certain levels of the ARBiH about the existence of soldiers in this sector. There's also, on our exhibit list - I don't have the exhibit number now in my head, but this is already an admitted exhibit - from the 10th of September, 1995, at midnight, an order issued by Mr. Hasanagic to the effect that searches of the terrain should be conducted in the sector of Pejanovici, a location which was encircled today, Kosa, another location which was encircled today, and Kesten, and the documents just shown, including this one, plus certain other documents, demonstrate, in the view of the Prosecution, that the existence of enemy soldiers at this point in time was known to the ARBiH. This is why this particular paragraph was highlighted today, and to be honest, I didn't intend to spend so much time, but I got several objections, as Your Honours could well observe, and therefore I spent much more time than initially envisaged on this particular document, but it needs to be read in context with other documents, including those which are shown today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you very much. This is very helpful to the Chamber, of course, because now we can see why you did it. I would have thought that you could have gotten there much faster, but the point, as I understand you correctly - if I understand you correctly - is to show that immediately after the liberation of this area by the ABiH, some 40 to 60 Serb soldiers were still running around in the woods, and they may or may not be captured, which we will see at a later point.

utterances.speaker: MR. NEUNER
utterances.text: Plus, Your Honours have seen that the documentation coming from 2nd Corps mentioning 100 soldiers, from 3rd Corps mentioning from 40 to 60, in this document which is now in front of Your Honours, you'll see it's a reinforced infantry battalion strength. I would have elucidated all these questions with the witness today, but as Your Honours could observe, I got a couple of objections. This witness, I can say, was in a position during proofing and on an earlier occasion to elucidate on this document, including he could give me exactly the strength of a reinforced infantry battalion. But with the objection, I don't want to say I got -- I was taken off guard, but the value of this document got sidetracked to a certain extent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Let's hope it does not happen again. Can I just ask for clarification. If the 100 documents observed by one corps and the 40 to 60 -- sorry, soldiers -- let me put this again.
